units: C (mean preferred temperature, Tsel, of frogs pooled over 15 populations; the quote prints the spread as +/- 2.18 without labelling it as SD or SE)
method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice: wild-caught frogs placed in a laboratory board gradient from 8 to 38 C, temperature selected recorded hourly, five readings per frog
conditions: Wild frogs from fifteen populations of Craugastor loki in the Sierra Madre de Chiapas, Mexico, collected in the rainy season (June to November) of 2017 and 2018, mostly at night (20:00 to 01:00) and occasionally by day; sex and adult status are not stated. Frogs were kept 3 days in plastic containers with their original substrate at laboratory temperature (about 23 C) and were not acclimated to another regime. Two thermal gradients (1.0 m x 0.8 m x 0.7 m high, wood boards), one end cooled to 8 C with ice packs and the other heated to 38 C with an electric hot plate; five frogs were placed in each gradient at a random location 1 h before the trials, which began at night at 21:00; each hour the Tsel of ten frogs (both gradients) was recorded, five readings per frog. Table 1 per-population n is 6 to 12 frogs; no total n is printed for the gradient trials. The same Results section (not in the quote) reports that Tsel varied with elevation and bioclimatic domain, that body size (SVL) was positively correlated with Tsel (smaller frogs selected lower temperatures), and that in populations above 1,100 m Tsel fell outside the range recorded for operative (Te) and body (Tb) temperatures in the field. The population means in the quote span 19.60 +/- 1.70 to 23.70 +/- 1.30 C. Single-sitting captive gradient choice, not a receptor threshold.

The Methods do not say how the five readings per frog were combined.

units: C (preferred temperature range, the interquartile range of preferred body temperature Tpref)
method: behavioural thermal-gradient choice: cloacal temperature of lizards in a laboratory glass terrarium gradient, 20 to 60 C
conditions: Wild adult lizards, 12 males and 12 females per species (n = 24 each), noosed during their daily activity period in the study area at the Natural Monument 'Lago de La Baña' (León province, Spain), 1,400 m asl; I. galani was tested in August 2011 and P. bocagei in August 2013, so the two species were not run in the same year. Housed individually in terraria, fed mealworms and crickets, water ad libitum; no acclimation period or fasting is reported. Glass terrarium gradient (100 x 60 x 60 cm) with a 150 W infrared lamp over one side, between 20 and 60 C; a cloacal temperature was taken with a digital thermometer each hour from 08:00 to 18:00 h (GMT), six hourly readings per lizard as the page tool summarised it (the eleven clock hours and six readings are not reconciled in the text read). The 'preferred temperature range' is defined in the Methods as the central 50% of preferred body temperatures (the interquartile range). Lizards were released at their capture sites afterwards. Same Results (not in the quote, read as separate sentences): mean Tpref of I. galani 28.8 +/- 0.47 C (n = 24) against 32.3 +/- 2.11 C for P. bocagei (Mann-Whitney U = 42.00, P < 0.0001); no sex difference in I. galani (males 28.9 +/- 0.48, females 28.8 +/- 0.49 C, n = 12 each, ANOVA P = 0.734); the I. galani range was significantly narrower than that of P. bocagei (Levene's test).
